Alex comes home feeling wrung out after the long evening. The apartment is quiet, and the familiar routine of putting away a coat and making tea helps the noise of the day fade. Alex goes to bed early, falls asleep easily, and sleeps soundly without interruption.

Morning light comes through the curtains. Alex wakes refreshed, clear-headed, and ready to enjoy being around people again. After breakfast and a leisurely shower, Alex lingers over another cup of tea at home, looking forward to seeing June later.

scenario.text:
The café is crowded and loud enough that Alex has to strain to follow June’s words. A difficult call from work keeps interrupting their conversation. Alex tries to stay present, but each interruption leaves them a little less able to engage. June notices the tired look on Alex’s face and gives them room to sit quietly.

By the time the rain eases, Alex is still at the table, rubbing tired eyes and struggling to focus on even a simple question. June is beside Alex, reading the menu while they take a breather. The two untouched menus lie between them as they listen to the last drops patter against the window.

### WHEN A COLLECTION CHANGES
For a new NPC, add starting entries only when the story or established background identifies them. A blank collection needs no output.
Report each collection change shown in the latest message:
- "remove" for consumption or loss; with quantity enabled, report the amount spent (default 1), or "all": true for the whole entry
- "add" for acquisitions, with the amount gained (default 1) when quantity is enabled; add newly demonstrated knowledge and abilities when missing
- "update" for changes to other item fields, with the identifier and changed values
The extension calculates remaining quantities and removes entries at zero. Reusable entries stay held after use.
For counted items, consumption uses "remove" with the identifier and amount spent. An "update" never changes quantity; do not put a quantity field there.
Follow collection purposes, targets, and field guidance. For abilities and knowledge, actual use establishes knowledge even when the outcome fails; add a missing entry when demonstrated. Include supported item details. Maintain one entry per identifier; quantity gains accumulate.
